title: Unit Economics Dashboard — Internal Demo Deck (Draft)
content:
Slide 1 — Title
Unit Economics Dashboard (Internal)
Standardizing blended cost of inference as $/1M output tokens

Speaker notes:
- Goal today: show the “source of truth” dashboard for unit economics, align on the metric definition, and walk through drilldowns + a few example insights.
- Audience: Finance (FP&A), Product, Platform/Telemetry, SRE.


Slide 2 — Why this exists
Problems we’re solving
- Multiple definitions of “cost per token” across teams
- Hard to explain why cost moved week-over-week (mix shift vs runtime changes)
- Inconsistent tie-out between telemetry-based metrics and billing/COGS reporting

What success looks like
- One canonical $/1M output tokens metric, finance-aligned
- Fast drilldowns by model / region / customer tier
- Built-in data quality guardrails + reconciliation

Speaker notes:
- This dashboard is intended to be used in weekly review and for day-to-day debugging when someone pings “cost is up.”


Slide 3 — Who uses it + key workflows
Users
- FP&A / Finance leadership: weekly KPI reporting, gross margin context, mix shift analysis
- Product: pricing/packaging decisions, routing defaults, rollout guardrails
- Engineering (Telemetry/Runtime/Infra): identify savings opportunities (batching/caching/quantization), regression detection
- SRE/Observability: data freshness & correctness alerts, incident response when pipelines drift

Workflows (we’ll demo)
1) Start at blended cost trend
2) Filter/slice by model / region / tier
3) Explain delta: attribute drivers (mix shift, cache hit rate, config adoption)
4) Validate data health + reconciliation status


Slide 4 — Canonical metric (top line)
Metric name (canonical)
Blended cost ($) per 1M output tokens

Displayed as
$/1M output tokens (daily, 7d rolling, and period summary)

Why output tokens
- Ties to primary “serving work” customers experience
- Reduces variance when prompts/input tokens shift across product surfaces

Speaker notes:
- We still capture input tokens + total tokens for context, but the headline KPI is output-based.


Slide 5 — Definition (high level)
Blended $/1M output tokens =
(Compute cost + Serving overhead allocation + Other infra-attributed cost) / (Output tokens / 1,000,000)

Compute cost includes
- GPU fleet cost allocated to inference workloads (hosted + dedicated + private, where applicable)
- Region-specific rates (cloud pricing differences, reserved capacity effects)

Overhead allocation (examples)
- Control plane + routing services
- Observability and data pipeline overhead (allocated)

Exclusions / non-goals (for now)
- R&D headcount (not part of COGS)
- Sales/CS costs

Speaker notes:
- We follow ADR-0142 for the exact inclusion/exclusion rules and allocation method.
- If something feels surprising, we’d rather make it explicit than hide it.


Slide 6 — Credits/discounts policy (how it shows up)
Two views (important)
1) Blended cost (COGS-like): ignores customer-specific discounting; focuses on what it costs us to serve
2) Net unit economics (restricted): incorporates credits/discount impacts for leadership + Finance only

Why separate
- Product/Engineering need a stable operational unit cost
- Finance needs both operational cost and margin context

Speaker notes:
- Access control is enforced (RBAC). If you don’t see the “Net” toggles, that’s expected.


Slide 7 — Dimensions & drilldowns (supported)
Core filters
- Time range (daily grain; week/month rollups)
- Model family + variant (e.g., llama-3.1-70b-instruct, mixtral-8x7b)
- Region (us-east, us-west, eu-west, ap-southeast)
- Customer tier: self_serve / dedicated / private / enterprise

Optional (MVP+)
- quantization_profile
- runtime_config (batching/caching preset)

Guardrails (to prevent cardinality blow-ups)
- Top-N limits on ad-hoc group-bys
- Some dimensions only available after selecting model family or tier

Speaker notes:
- The goal is “fast and correct,” not “infinite pivot table.”


Slide 8 — Dashboard layout (1/3): Overview tab
Overview tab shows
- KPI tiles: blended $/1M output tokens, output tokens, GPU-hours, cache hit rate
- Trend chart with comparisons: WoW / MoM / vs trailing 28d average
- Breakdown: cost composition (compute vs overhead)

Primary question answered
- “Is unit cost trending up/down, and is it compute-driven or overhead-driven?”


Slide 9 — Dashboard layout (2/3): Drilldowns tab
Drilldowns tab shows
- Table: $/1M output tokens by (model x region) with tier filter
- Mini-trends per row (sparkline) + delta vs previous period
- Click-through to a detail page for the slice

Primary question answered
- “Which model/region/tier is driving the change?”

Speaker notes:
- This is where Product typically lives when asking about routing defaults.


Slide 10 — Dashboard layout (3/3): Explain tab (“cost delta”)
Explain tab shows
- Period A vs Period B comparison
- Driver decomposition (waterfall)
  - Model mix shift
  - Region mix shift
  - Cache hit-rate change (and estimated savings impact)
  - Quantization profile adoption shift
  - Residual (unexplained)

Primary question answered
- “What changed, and how much did each driver contribute?”

Speaker notes:
- Residual is a feature, not a bug: it tells us where we need better attribution or if a runtime change occurred.


Slide 11 — Data lineage (trust story)
Data sources (conceptual)
- Metering events: tokens (input/output), model_id, region, tier, tags (quantization_profile, runtime_config)
- Cost inputs: fleet costs by region + day (GPU-hour rate curves, reserved capacity effects)
- Allocation tables: overhead allocation rules by day/tier/region

Pipeline principles
- Partitioned by day (daily aggregates are the stability layer)
- Late-arriving events handled via controlled backfills
- Reconciliation job runs daily and flags variance

Speaker notes:
- We intentionally built a semantic layer rather than one-off queries.


Slide 12 — Freshness/completeness SLOs
SLOs (targets)
- Freshness: daily partition available by 09:00 local time (region-aware), with partials earlier
- Completeness: >= 99.5% of expected metering events within 24h (by region/tier)
- Reconciliation: dashboard totals vs billing/metering totals within agreed tolerance

Alerts & routing
- Freshness / completeness alerts -> #eng-sre + #eng-platform
- Reconciliation variance alerts -> #eng-platform + Finance point of contact (FP&A)

Speaker notes:
- When the dashboard is “wrong,” it should be loudly wrong (banner + alert), not silently wrong.


Slide 13 — Reconciliation (what we compare)
Daily reconciliation compares
- Dashboard: aggregated tokens + allocated costs
vs
- Billing hooks / metering totals: tokens + billable usage totals

How variance is displayed
- Traffic-light status (OK / Watch / Fail)
- Top variance contributors (region/tier)
- Notes field for known incidents (e.g., late partitions, mapping changes)

Speaker notes:
- Expect small differences due to timing; we’re aligned on tolerance and escalation thresholds.


Slide 14 — Demo flow (live)
We’ll do three mini-demos
1) “Cost is up 8% WoW” -> find the driver
2) “eu-west mismatch” -> validate reconciliation + mapping
3) “Quant rollout” -> show savings and quality caveats

Speaker notes:
- We’ll use last 14 days in the demo environment and show a few saved views.


Slide 15 — Example insight #1: model mix shift drives unit cost
Scenario
- Blended $/1M output tokens increased WoW

What we found
- Traffic shifted from llama-3.1-8b to llama-3.1-70b for a subset of enterprise routes
- Output tokens stable overall, but GPU-hours per 1M output tokens increased

Dashboard steps
- Overview -> see spike
- Drilldowns -> group by model family
- Explain -> “model mix shift” accounts for majority of delta

Action
- Product: validate routing policy intent + communicate tradeoff
- Eng: confirm runtime configs are consistent across variants


Slide 16 — Example insight #2: region mix + fleet rate change
Scenario
- US regions flat, eu-west $/1M output tokens up

What we found
- Increased eu-west share + higher effective GPU-hour rate due to capacity constraints
- Dedicated tier in eu-west was overrepresented in the spike window

Dashboard steps
- Filter: region=eu-west
- Compare: current 7d vs previous 7d
- Explain -> region/tier mix and compute-rate component

Action
- Infra: revisit eu-west capacity plan / reservation coverage
- Product: consider routing fallback thresholds to reduce expensive spill


Slide 17 — Example insight #3: cache hit rate regression
Scenario
- Sudden cost spike without corresponding traffic increase

What we found
- Prefix/KV cache hit rate dropped for a major self_serve workload
- Estimated “cache savings” decreased (dashboard shows negative contribution)

Dashboard steps
- Overview -> cache hit rate tile down
- Drilldowns -> isolate by route/config (if enabled)
- Explain -> cache component accounts for material delta

Action
- Runtime/Platform: check cache keying changes, TTL, and eviction pressure
- SRE: correlate with deployment timeline / incidents


Slide 18 — Example insight #4: quantization profile adoption
Scenario
- Gradual improvement in blended $/1M output tokens for a model family

What we found
- Higher adoption of quantization_profile=q4_k_m for llama-3.1-70b in us-east
- Savings visible as lower GPU-hours per 1M output tokens

Caveat
- Must be interpreted alongside quality metrics / eval gates (not in this dashboard)

Action
- Applied ML: confirm quality guardrails
- Product: adjust default profile recommendation if stable

Speaker notes:
- This is why quantization_profile tagging and versioning matter.


Slide 19 — Common questions (pre-emptive)
Q: Why output tokens and not total tokens?
- Output tokens best captures serving cost drivers; we still expose total tokens and input tokens in details.

Q: Can I export?
- Yes: CSV export for tables + shareable slice links (internal).

Q: How do we handle late data?
- Daily partitions can be reprocessed; dashboard shows a “data updated” marker and reconciliation status.

Q: Can I see account-level cost?
- Not in this dashboard (by design). Restricted views are tier-based only; account-level analysis is separate and gated.


Slide 20 — Known limitations (MVP)
- Some high-cardinality slicing is intentionally disabled (route-level pivots) until performance is validated
- Private deployments: cost attribution coverage varies by customer integration maturity
- Residual in Explain tab can be large during periods of rapid change (new model onboardings, region bring-ups)

Speaker notes:
- Please file issues with concrete examples: time range, filter set, screenshot, and expected behavior.


Slide 21 — Rollout plan + feedback
Rollout
- Behind internal feature flag initially
- Staged enablement: Finance + Product leads -> broader Eng

Feedback channels
- #eng-platform for pipeline/data issues
- #product-console for UX requests
- Linear epic: PM-482 (comment with screenshots + slice links)

Success metrics (first 4 weeks)
- Weekly unit econ review uses this dashboard as primary source
- Reconciliation pass rate >= target threshold
- Time-to-explain cost spike: < 30 minutes for common scenarios


Slide 22 — Appendix: where to find the spec / ADR
Reference docs
- ADR: canonical blended $/1M output token definition (ADR-0142)
- Data contracts: dimensions, freshness SLOs, owners
- SLO doc: pipeline freshness/completeness/reconciliation thresholds

Implementation references
- Aggregation job PR: redwood/pr-11842
- Reconciliation PR: redwood/pr-11871
- Console UI PR: redwood/pr-11879

Speaker notes:
- If something in the dashboard contradicts ADR-0142, treat it as a bug and flag it.


Slide 23 — Appendix: demo checklist (for presenter)
Before demo
- Confirm today’s partition status = green
- Have 2 saved views ready:
  - “All traffic — last 14d”
  - “eu-west / dedicated — last 14d”
- Pull up reconciliation panel in separate tab

During demo
- Always narrate the filter state (model/region/tier)
- Call out data freshness banner if present

After demo
- Post link + known limitations in #announcements once launch is approved
